mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where this trigger occurs, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a tech-driven market rally.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect disappears during a strong earnings season.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during a global supply shock that boosts commodity prices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, increasing real interest rates and eroding corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such co-occurrences, or the effect is absent during a market rally driven by fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered events, or the effect is reversed during a surge in mortgage rates that boosts bank earnings.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows positive and increasing 1-month changes for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the effect disappears during a sector-specific sell-off.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and real retail sales (RSAFS) for three consecutive months indicates a broad-based slowdown in economic activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases uncertainty, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and RSAFS both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes, or the effect is reversed during a sharp rebound in global demand.
